$comment: WHAT THIS CHECKS, AND WHY IT IS A SEPARATE CONFIG
The build (tsconfig.json) only covers src/**/*.ts. That left two kinds of
JavaScript checked by nothing -- not by tsc, not by a linter:
bin/cli.mjs   the `bin` entry in package.json, shipped verbatim via
`files`, i.e. the one file every `npx agentlens` executes
scripts/      the merge-gate machinery itself: ci-contexts.mjs derives
the required status-check context names, and
check-live-protection.mjs asserts the LIVE ruleset matches
them. A type error here does not reach an npm consumer, but
it decides whether `main` is protected at all, which is a
worse blast radius, not a smaller one.
It is a separate file rather than folded into tsconfig.json because
rootDir: src + outDir: dist cannot also emit for bin/ (TS6059), and because
this config must not emit: bin/cli.mjs is published verbatim. (noEmit is
correct hygiene rather than a load-bearing safety net -- tsc actually
refuses with TS5055 'would overwrite input file' even under --noEmit false.
The option stays; the previous comment's claim that it prevents an
otherwise-possible clobber was overstated.)
WHAT IT CATCHES -- measured, by injecting each defect and running the gate
Property typos against the imported Trace/Span types (TS2551/TS2339),
wrong arity in both directions (TS2554), wrong-typed arguments (TS2345), a
missing await (TS2345), dereferencing the nullable durationMs (TS18047),
bad module specifiers and bad named imports (TS2307/TS2724), undeclared
identifiers (TS2304), and comparisons against a string union with no
overlap (TS2367).
WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH -- stated because the previous version of this
comment claimed the opposite
An earlier revision justified this whole config with 'a typo in an argv
branch ships to npm while CI stays green'. That was false: argv dispatch
was a switch over a plain string, which carries no exhaustiveness
obligation, so a misspelled `case`, a misspelled flag literal and a
wrongly-wired handler all passed with exit 0. Part of that gap is now
closed in code rather than in prose -- bin/cli.mjs dispatches through a
`Record<Command, CommandHandler>` table, so a misspelled or unhandled
command name IS a compile error (TS2353/TS2741). What types still cannot
see, because the three handlers are structurally identical and any string
is a valid comparison operand: the WRONG handler wired to a correct name,
and a misspelled FLAG literal. test/cli.test.mjs covers both by running the
built binary over the real command surface. The compiler is also
Node-version-blind (@types/node is one version, engines.node is >=20); the
matrix job is what covers that.
SCOPE -- real numbers, measured at this commit, not copied forward
Widening the include to examples/ + test/ adds 60 errors (examples/ 9,
test/ 51), overwhelmingly implicit-any and possibly-undefined in fixtures.
They are excluded for cost, not on the principle the old comment stated ('a
type error there cannot reach a consumer') -- that framing is wrong for
test/, where checkJs is the only tool that flags
`assert.throws(fn, "string")`,
which Node treats as the assertion's own message and which therefore
accepts ANY error. One such call existed in
test/ci-contexts-mutations.test.mjs and is fixed; typing test/ properly is
a worthwhile separate pass.
EXTENSIONS -- why the include is six entries and not one brace glob
`files: ["dist","bin","README.md"]` publishes the whole bin/ DIRECTORY,
not just the one path package.json#bin names. An earlier revision globbed
`bin/**/*.mjs` only, and that was declined as theoretical on the grounds
that package.json#bin has a single entry. Measured: a bin/helper.js holding
two blatant type errors (an implicit-any parameter dereferenced as
x.nope.toUpperCase(), and a number multiplied by a string) left
`npm run typecheck:bin` at exit 0 with the gate's own self-test still
passing 4/4. A sibling helper next to the entrypoint is one `git add` away
and is the LIKELIER case than renaming the entrypoint, so the narrow glob
was a live hole in the publish surface, not a theoretical one.
The obvious one-line fix -- `bin/**/*.{mjs,js,cjs}` -- does NOT work and
was rejected by measurement, not taste: tsc's include globs support only
*, ? and **, not brace alternation, so that pattern matches a literal
directory name and the config dies with
`error TS18003: No inputs were found`. Six explicit entries it is.
DO NOT WIDEN OR NARROW THIS SILENTLY. test/typecheck-gate.test.mjs reads
this file, asserts the load-bearing options are present, resolves the
include against package.json#bin, asserts package.json's typecheck:bin
SCRIPT still points `tsc -p` at this exact file, and -- the real backstop --
copies the repo into a sandbox, plants type defects into the REAL
bin/cli.mjs and into new bin/*.js and bin/*.cjs siblings, and runs the
unmodified `npm run typecheck:bin` script there, requiring each defect to be
REPORTED by name. Deleting `checkJs` here, narrowing this include,
suppressing checking at the top of the entrypoint, or repointing the script
at a permissive config are all test failures -- each one was injected and
observed failing, not assumed.
